observed_sdk_path: DistributedApplicationTestingBuilder.DelegatedHost.StopAsync awaits testing-factory disposal with the caller token.
DistributedApplicationFactory sets DcpPublisher:WaitForResourceCleanup=true and reads HostOptions.ShutdownTimeout from the built host (live value: 30 seconds).
Factory disposal bounds entry-point exit, application StopAsync and DisposeAsync using that shutdown token; cancellation may complete the wrapper before a child process exit is visible.
DcpExecutor.StopAsync cancels watchers, optionally awaits CleanupResourcesAsync, and requests a Full orchestrator stop; it catches cancellation and logs other failures at Debug.

KubernetesService.CleanupResourcesAsync patches CleaningResources/Full and polls ResourcesCleanedUp; ordering is delegated to DCP, whose exact source does not order Executable cleanup before Container cleanup.
DcpExecutor.DisposeAsync uses a ten-second cancellation budget for StopAsync.
DcpExecutor.StopResourceAsync patches only the selected executable Stop flag and waits for Finished/Terminated, leaving backing containers intact.
fixture_repair: Stop owned project hosts concurrently while sidecars and backing containers remain available, then stop owned executables/sidecars concurrently; re-observe and repeat within the same token for late partial-start workers. On Linux read /proc/PID/stat state and start-clock ticks directly, treating zombies as exited and rejecting reused PID identities. Only after exact worker quiescence and the optional test observer may the fully awaited testing-host disposal remove backing containers. One cumulative 30-second worker-quiescence budget covers stop passes, exit observations, the observer and automatic fallback within a cleanup attempt. Preserve app, builder, identities and control-plane ownership on failure; a later explicit retry gets its own attempt. An unsuccessful SDK stop can be resolved only by independent exit of its exact captured OS process.
inspection_commands: dnx dotnet-inspect -y -- member Aspire.Hosting.DistributedApplication --package Aspire.Hosting@13.6.1 -m StopAsync -v:d -n 120
observation_issue: The original apparent survivor was an observation false positive: DCP reported executables Finished and independent /proc checks showed all recorded PIDs absent, while cached non-child Process observations timed out. Even opening another Process instance can share that cached wait state. The Linux kernel identity probe replaces it; a focused grandchild-process regression retains a .NET handle across live, mismatched-lifetime and actual-exit checks. This observation issue is separate from the source-proven absence of worker-before-container ordering in DCP.
budget_limits: The 30-second worker-quiescence budget is cumulative for one cleanup attempt. Existing SDK host/factory shutdown and control-plane script budgets remain distinct; passing live tests observe total cleanup below 60 seconds, rather than asserting an unconditional global 60-second bound.

dcp_source.ordering: Container cleanup depends on ContainerExec only; Executable cleanup depends on ExecutableReplicaSet only. There is no executable-before-container cleanup dependency. Fully awaited SDK cleanup alone therefore does not establish the frozen backing-resource ordering.
